title: Commit Secret Guard
summary: Scans the lines a diff adds for keys, passwords and high-entropy strings, so credentials are noticed before they go into a commit.
description: Scans only added diff lines for provider keys, private keys, passwords in URLs, hard-coded secrets and high-entropy strings, flags .env and key files, skips test fixtures by pattern (except live key formats), and offers per-finding fixes, warning to rotate if already pushed.
catches: Provider key formats (AWS, GitHub, Stripe, OpenAI, Slack and others) and private keys
Passwords embedded in URLs and hard-coded secrets
High-entropy strings that look like tokens
.env and key files added to the commit
Changes already pushed, with a rotate-now link for the provider
limits: Pattern and entropy based: it can miss custom secret formats and flag random-looking test data
Only scans the diff you pass; history and other branches are not checked
Marking a false positive is your call; it does not verify the key is inactive
a11y: Findings are a labelled list that can receive focus
Focus moves to the next unresolved finding or the commit button
Each finding states its file, line and kind in text
Rotate links open in a new tab with rel="noreferrer noopener"
server: Run secret scanning in CI or as a pre-receive hook, and rotate any credential that was pushed.
